task: Review this patient-facing explanation from a synthetic risk-literacy exercise, not a real clinical study. Explain the unsupported conversion from relative risk to an absolute number and identify the missing information. Preserve the supplied relative comparison without recommending treatment, inventing a baseline, or supplying an illustrative baseline as though it were observed.
input: The summary reports a 20 percent relative reduction in the chance of the outcome. That means 20 fewer people in every 100 will have it.

facts.text: The teaching packet defines a 20 percent relative reduction for an unnamed outcome.
The baseline risk of that outcome is not supplied.
The packet does not supply an absolute outcome count.
The packet does not specify a follow-up period.

forbidden_additions: An invented baseline risk, absolute risk reduction, or number needed to treat.
The claim of 20 fewer people per 100 treated as established.
A treatment name, recommendation, population, or follow-up period not in the packet.
preserve: The distinction between a relative reduction and percentage-point or person-count differences.
The fact that missing baseline information prevents the claimed absolute conversion.
